executive_summary.text: In Q3 2026 INFANT saw strong growth in Instagram reach (+282.1% YoY) and Facebook activity (+839% YoY views), while publication output fell sharply (‑54% QoQ). Email engagement remained high (46.7% best‑performing campaign). KPI reporting increased but many presentation‑related KPIs declined. Data gaps limit insight into website and event calendars.

key_findings.statement: Instagram reach (daily figures added up) rose to 26,225, a +282.1% increase from Q3 2025 but fell 2% from Q2 2026.
Facebook views jumped to 68,289, a +839.3% increase YoY, while visits fell 7.4% QoQ.
Verified publications dropped to 11, a 54.2% decline QoQ and 38.9% YoY.

kpi_analysis.interpretation: KPI reporting increased 30.4% QoQ to 30 recorded KPIs, but the total tracker holds 85 KPIs, indicating partial coverage.
Poster presentations fell to 7, a 63.2% drop QoQ, suggesting reduced conference activity.
Oral presentations fell to 4, a 73.3% drop QoQ, reinforcing the trend of fewer presentations.
New research staff rose to 5, a 150% increase QoQ, indicating recruitment momentum.
Current research staff held steady at 63 (0% YoY change).
Funding secured fell to €1 million, a 47.6% decline YoY.

website.summary: Website data not connected; no analysis possible.

social.summary: Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn showed mixed performance with notable reach growth but modest interaction changes.

findings.statement: Instagram reach (daily figures added up) increased 282.1% YoY to 26,225 but fell 2% QoQ.
Facebook interactions rose 51.2% QoQ to 3,921, while visits declined 7.4% QoQ.

email.summary: Eleven campaigns were sent with strong open (45.7%) and engagement (11.7%) rates.

findings.statement: Best‑performing campaign achieved 60.0% open rate and 46.7% engagement rate.
Overall email open rate was 45.7% and click‑to‑open rate 25.6%.

content.summary: No post‑level content data for the period.

media.summary: Press and media mentions increased to 9 entries (27 total mentions) after a zero baseline in Q2 2026.

findings.statement: Media entries rose to 9, with total mentions of 27 for the quarter.

publications.summary: Publication output declined sharply, with 11 verified papers and 63.6% open‑access share.

findings.statement: Publications fell 54.2% QoQ to 11; open‑access share was 63.6%.

events.summary: One Eventbrite event was held with capacity for 1,100 participants.

findings.statement: Ev.1992827849744 (Roar for Research) completed on 2026‑08‑08 with 1,100 capacity.

conferences.summary: No conference data for the period.

kpis.summary: KPI reporting improved, but many presentation‑related KPIs declined; staff numbers remained stable.

findings.statement: KPI reporting increased 30.4% QoQ to 30 recorded KPIs.
Poster and oral presentation KPIs fell sharply QoQ.

trends.statement: Social media reach metrics (Instagram, Facebook) show strong YoY growth, while interaction metrics are relatively flat QoQ.

cross_dataset.statement: Increased social media reach coincides with higher email engagement rates, suggesting coordinated digital outreach.

risks.statement: Publication output decline may affect research visibility and funding prospects.
Small bases for many KPI changes (e.g., poster presentations) limit reliability of trend conclusions.

opportunities.statement: Rapid Instagram reach growth offers a platform to amplify research dissemination and stakeholder engagement.
High email engagement rates indicate potential to expand targeted communications for fundraising and collaborations.

recommendations.recommendation: Leverage the Instagram reach surge by scheduling regular research highlights and calls for collaboration on the platform.
recommendations.reasoning: Reach growth provides audience exposure; consistent content can translate reach into engagement and partnerships.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Increased stakeholder awareness and potential collaborations

recommendations.recommendation: Address the publication decline by allocating dedicated writing support and setting quarterly output targets.
recommendations.reasoning: Sustained research output is linked to visibility and funding; support can mitigate the downward trend.

recommendations.recommendation: Standardise KPI tracking to reduce reliance on small comparison bases and improve data reliability.
recommendations.reasoning: Small bases undermine confidence in trend analysis; consistent tracking will enable clearer performance assessment.

limitations: All figures were calculated by the dashboard from the sources above. The AI interpreted them but did not calculate any number, and every figure it quotes was checked against the data; any problems found are shown with the report.
Where a period was not fully covered by data, comparisons use the same number of days in each period.
Instagram reach adds up each day's reach, so one account can be counted on several days; it is not the number of unique accounts reached.
Follower figures are new followers gained, not net growth: people who unfollowed are not subtracted.
Changes between periods show association, not cause.
